newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GBL says eyes more PetroFina.
newsitem.headline: GBL says eyes more PetroFina.

text.p: Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA said on Tuesday it was still looking to increase its stake in Belgian oil group PetroFina, despite the fact it will be diluted as the result of an ongoing capital increase.
GBL presently holds a 22.8 percent stake in PetroFina through its Electrafina unit.

"The (present) warrants exercise will mean our stake is diluted by around one percent. But in time, using opportunities that arise, we will probably strengthen it again," GBL chairman Albert Frere told the annual shareholders meeting.
The 1,162,611 PetroFina warrants, giving their holders the right to acquire one PetroFina share at 12,500 francs, can be exercised until June 3. The exercise period started on May 20.
Electrafina chief executive officer Thierry de Rudder told the assembly the company had sold all the warrants it held in PetroFina.

Frere said, however, this did not mean GBL believed PetroFina was overvalued and it could buy the shares at a lower price at a later date. If opportunities arose, GBL could also pay 12,500 francs a share to increase its stake, he said.
De Rudder said it was Electrafina's long-term objective to buy around 25 percent of the oil group. He noted that when the objective was set in 1990 Electrafina held around 20 percent of PetroFina.
PetroFina has been one of the least performing companies in the GBL portfolio and on the Brussels bourse since 1991, according to figures published in GBL's annual report.
At April 15, 1997, PetroFina's share price was only worth 15 percent more than it was in 1990, GBL said. At the same date, GBL's share was worth 54 percent more than in 1991.

PetroFina has said it will use the approximate 14.5 billion Belgian francs it will gain if all warrants are exercised to fund its planned buyout of minority shareholders in its U.S. Fina Inc unit. PetroFina already owns 85 percent of Fina.
